why: Knowing the length and order of each section lets you set a per-question pace before test day.
rule:
The current test takes about 1 hour 58 minutes and has five sections.

- **Analytical Writing**: one Analyze an Issue task, 30 minutes. Always first.
- **Verbal Reasoning**: section 1 has 12 questions in 18 minutes, section 2 has 15 in 23.
- **Quantitative Reasoning**: section 1 has 12 questions in 21 minutes, section 2 has 15 in 26.

Verbal and Quantitative sections can appear in any order after Writing. Before September 22, 2023 the test was longer (about 3 hours 45 minutes, 20 questions per section); do not use old figures.

examples.prompt: What is the total allotted time?
About how long can you spend on each question of the second Quantitative section (15 questions, 26 minutes)?

trap: Using the pre-September 2023 format (two writing tasks, 20 questions per section) or assuming Quant always follows Verbal. Only Writing's position is fixed.

checks.stem: How many questions are in the first Verbal Reasoning section?
checks.explanation: The first Verbal section has 12 questions in 18 minutes.

choiceExplanations.C: That is the second Verbal section.
choiceExplanations.D: That is the first section's time in minutes.

checks.stem: How many minutes in total are allotted to the two Quantitative sections?
A test-taker finishes Analytical Writing and sees a Verbal section next. Which statement is correct?

choices.text: This is impossible; Quant must follow Writing.
This is possible; Verbal and Quant sections may appear in any order after Writing.
This is impossible; Writing is always last.
This is a mistake in the test.
Only an unscored section can follow Writing.

choiceExplanations.D: Any order after Writing is allowed.
